package.description: Optional Revised Section 508 Standards package for ART. This package is not part of ART built-in standards.
package.author: U.S. Access Board
package.license: Public Domain / official government source summaries
package.legalScope: Implementation aid only; this package does not determine legal applicability or compliance.
package.contentPolicy: Original summaries and links are provided instead of reproducing the official standard text.
package.notes: Requirement summaries are intentionally concise and link to the official source. Full official regulatory text and copyrighted/incorporated materials are not reproduced. Human Section 508 and Trusted Tester review remains required before production claims.

standards.scopeSummary: The Revised 508 Standards apply to covered information and communication technology procured, developed, maintained, or used by covered U.S. federal agencies, subject to the rule's scope and exceptions.

incorporatedStandards.name: WCAG 2.0
incorporatedStandards.scope: Web content, software, and electronic documents are addressed through the incorporated accessibility requirements identified by the Revised 508 Standards.

chapters.title: Application and Administration
chapters.summary: Defines how the standards are organized and administered, including application and referenced terms.

chapters.title: Scoping Requirements
chapters.summary: Describes covered ICT, exclusions, exceptions, and how requirements apply to ICT components and support documentation.

chapters.title: Functional Performance Criteria
chapters.summary: Provides technology-independent outcomes for users with different functional limitations when detailed technical provisions do not fully address a situation.

chapters.title: Hardware
chapters.summary: Addresses hardware features, controls, indicators, ports, and interoperability with assistive technology.

chapters.title: Software
chapters.summary: Addresses software accessibility, user controls, interoperability, keyboard operation, and user interface behavior.

chapters.title: Support Documentation and Services
chapters.summary: Addresses accessible product documentation, support services, and communication channels.

chapters.title: Referenced Standards
chapters.summary: Identifies external technical standards incorporated by reference and their relationship to the Revised 508 requirements.

testingLifecycle.label: Plan
testingLifecycle.summary: Define the ICT scope, users, environments, applicable provisions, and evidence needed.

testingLifecycle.label: Test
testingLifecycle.summary: Use appropriate automated, manual, assistive-technology, and code-inspection techniques.

testingLifecycle.label: Remediate
testingLifecycle.summary: Record failures, prioritize risk, assign owners, and verify fixes.

testingLifecycle.label: Monitor
testingLifecycle.summary: Retest changes and maintain accessibility evidence across the ICT lifecycle.

trustedTester.methodology: Trusted Tester is a repeatable manual web accessibility test process that uses code inspection and browser/assistive-technology checks to complement automated testing.
trustedTester.trainingAndCertification: Training, tester qualification, and any certification or program requirements are maintained by the responsible program and are not provided by ART.

resultOptions.label: Pass
resultOptions.meaning: The applicable test was performed and the requirement was satisfied.

resultOptions.label: Fail
resultOptions.meaning: The applicable test was performed and the requirement was not satisfied.

resultOptions.label: Not Applicable
resultOptions.meaning: The requirement does not apply under the documented scope.

resultOptions.label: Not Tested
resultOptions.meaning: The applicable test has not yet been performed.

standards.applicabilityRules: Structured applicability metadata is provided for the package foundation; authoritative scoping review is required before production use.

criteria.title: Without Vision
criteria.desc: ICT must provide at least one mode of operation that does not require user vision.
criteria.failures: Critical workflows require visual-only cues with no non-visual equivalent.
criteria.fixes: Expose equivalent information and control through programmatic interfaces and assistive technologies.

criteria.title: With Limited Vision
criteria.desc: ICT must support users with limited vision, including contrast, zoom, and scalable text behaviors.
criteria.failures: Interfaces fail at high zoom or low-vision settings.
criteria.fixes: Preserve readability, layout integrity, and control operability at high zoom levels.

criteria.title: Without Perception of Color
criteria.desc: Color must not be the only visual means of conveying information.
criteria.failures: Status is conveyed by color alone.
criteria.fixes: Add text labels, patterns, icons, or equivalent non-color cues.

criteria.title: With Limited Manipulation
criteria.desc: ICT must support operation by users with limited fine motor control and reach.
criteria.failures: Controls require precise pointer movement or timing.
criteria.fixes: Provide keyboard operation, adequate target size, and alternatives to precision gestures.

criteria.title: Without Speech
criteria.desc: ICT should provide an effective mode of operation that does not require speech when speech is not available or cannot be used.
criteria.failures: A workflow requires spoken input or output with no effective non-speech alternative.
criteria.fixes: Provide equivalent text, visual, keyboard, or other non-speech interaction where the workflow requires it.

criteria.title: Software and Assistive Technology Interoperability
criteria.desc: Software should expose information, relationships, states, and operations through platform accessibility services or other supported interoperability mechanisms.
criteria.failures: Assistive technology cannot obtain or operate important user interface information.
criteria.fixes: Use platform accessibility APIs and preserve programmatic names, roles, states, values, and relationships.

criteria.title: Support Documentation and Services
criteria.desc: Product documentation and support services should be available in accessible formats and through accessible communication channels.
criteria.failures: Users cannot obtain accessible documentation or use the support channel with assistive technology.
criteria.fixes: Provide accessible documentation, contact methods, and alternate formats appropriate to the ICT and its users.
